recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not restore the deleted core source/icd.html page or duplicate the ICD combination-syntax prose in FHIR core; future changes to this guidance should be made in THO/UTG unless the Vocabulary WG decides to bring the content back into core.
issue_request: FHIR-12278 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for DSTU2 and asked FHIR to document the ISO 21090 ICD combination syntax as a base part of the ICD-10 code system, covering dual/multiple coding use cases, display guidance for expressions, and applicability to ICD-9, ICD-10, ICD-O, and variants.
initial_application: SVN-derived commit 7e7c737ad added a source/terminologies-systems.html note that ICD dual coding uses two ICD-10 codes separated by a space such as J21.8 B95.6. Commit 256d5061c then expanded the guidance into source/icd.html with a Dual Coding section, rationale bullets, and the J21.8/B95.6 example matching the Jira comments.
additional_context: FHIR-13210 later refined the same ICD multiple-coding guidance to preserve modifier characters such as +, *, and ! when present. FHIR-35933 moved the Using X external code-system pages, including source/icd.html, from FHIR core to THO, and current FHIR core keeps only the active terminologies-systems.html row that links to the authoritative THO Using ICD-[x] page.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit. No FHIR core source change was made because the current core source correctly delegates ICD syntax details to THO and the current THO ICD page contains the FHIR-12278 substance, including dual/multiple coding as a Coding.code expression and the J21.8 B95.6 example.

related_jiras.note: Later ICD multiple-coding issue expanded the same guidance to preserve +, *, and ! modifiers; it is already represented on the combined branch.
Moved Using X external code-system pages from FHIR core to THO and explains why the detailed ICD syntax page is no longer maintained in this checkout.
